newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil state tackles Banerj pension fund issue.
newsitem.headline: Brazil state tackles Banerj pension fund issue.

text.p: The future owner of Brazil's Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj will have to present an identical pension fund as the one now in place for existing employees, the state Planning Secretary said.
But in a statement today, secretary Marcelo Aurelio Alencar said a plan for former workers would be absorbed by the state.
"The state will have the responsibility for the management of a plan for previous Banerj workers," Alencar said.
Pension funds have been cited as a reason Banerj's privatisation, now scheduled to take place on December 26, may not actually take place this year.
A 650 million reais debt the bank owes a pension fund has been seen as making investors wary of the Banerj sale.
The new date for the privatisation was announced today after the state government succeeded in lifting a court injunction that blocked the original auction, due to have taken place December 17.
The injunction had been granted to the Association of Banerj's employees, an opponent of the sell-off.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
